If ‘R % T & Z $ S @ V @ C % Y’, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: C is the paternal grandmother of Z.
T is the mother of S.
T is the daughter of C.
V is the father of Z.

questions.solution:
Preparing the family tree using the following symbols:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/599c31a3b6c5ca06ce1787b908a152975e0540fada6e60ee63a4282f38f5a661.png] 

 ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’.

‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’.

‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’.

‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’.

 
 

 **Symbol**
 %
 $
 @
 &
 
 

 **Meaning**
 sister
 brother
 son
 mother
 
 

The given expression is :

‘R % T & Z $ S @ V @ C % Y’ → R is sister of T, T is mother of Z, Z is brother of S, S is son of V, V is the son of C, C is the sister of Y.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a6db76463cd9bd1395a7ae6eb187436a37b4f635810901f3e7fe748ed88e0c41.png] 

Option 1) : C is the paternal grandmother of Z → True (As T is mother of Z, Z is brother of S, S is son of V, V is the son of C so, C is the paternal grandmother of Z is true)

Option 2) : T is the mother of S → True (As T is mother of Z, Z is brother of S, S is son of V so, T is the mother of S is true)

Option 3) : T is the daughter of C → False (As T is mother of Z, Z is brother of S, S is son of V, V is the son of C so, **T is daughter-in-law of C** but given T is the daughter of C is false)

Option 4) : V is the father of Z → True (As T is mother of Z, Z is brother of S, S is son of V so, V is the father of Z is true)

∴ Here, 'T is the daughter of C' is not correct by following statements in given expression.

Hence, the correct answer is **"T is the daughter of C".**

Now break the code ‘T × V + Z’

**1) ****T × V**
